LanguageData.CC_Settings_AnswersPlayOut: Answers play out on the map
LanguageData.CC_Settings_AnswersPlayOut_Tip:
When the council's answer to a dilemma or an event describes something people do, they do it. A victory feast is eaten at the dining table from the colony's own cooked meals, a bonfire is lit and gathered round, a toast is raised, someone goes to sit with a friend, by a grave or at the camp's fire, a student works at a teacher's side, a worn-out doctor is sent to bed. A work party cleans, hauls, mends or sows together, mourners walk out to a grave and back, a watch is kept at the gate through the night, searchers go out over the land, medicine sent to a neighbor is carried out to the rider at the gate, the hunters go after the game. The moods the answer gives come to those who took part, once it's over.

Nobody is pulled away from danger, sleep, a meal or a sickbed, and nothing starts while enemies are about; anyone drafted, hungry or worn out is let go. If it can't happen within a few hours, the moods come anyway, as they always did, and what was to be carried out leaves the stores all the same.

Off: answers give their moods and messages only.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_AnswersPlayOut: Feasts, visits, work parties, vigils and errands happen on the map; the moods follow for those there.
